summary: Adds the BGP communities attribute, a tag that can be attached to routes so neighboring and distant networks can group them and apply policy to the whole group. It gives operators a simple way to signal their routing wishes.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 1997 adds a tag, called a community, to BGP routes. Routers can match the tag and apply one policy to every route that carries it. This replaces long lists of address prefixes with a single group label.

how does the communities attribute work
subtitle: A tag on BGP routes that lets operators group destinations and apply policy to the whole group.

tldr.problem: BGP policy was controlled only by matching IP address prefixes or the AS_PATH attribute, which made configuration large and slow to maintain.
tldr.mechanism: The COMMUNITIES path attribute (type code 8) carries a set of 32-bit values, so a route can be tagged and policy can match the group instead of long prefix lists.
tldr.outcome: It defines the well-known values NO_EXPORT, NO_ADVERTISE and NO_EXPORT_SUBCONFED, and it has been updated by RFC 7606 and RFC 8642.

today: RFC 1997 is a Proposed Standard. It was updated by RFC 7606 and RFC 8642, and it has not been obsoleted.

sections.title: Grouping Destinations
sections.content:
Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) supports transit policies by controlling how routing information is distributed, but that control was based on IP address prefixes or on the value of the AS_PATH attribute. RFC 1997 suggests grouping destinations so a routing decision can also rest on a group identity. A community is a group of destinations that share some common property. Each autonomous system administrator defines which communities a destination belongs to; by default, every destination belongs to the general Internet community.

The RFC gives two examples. An operator could tag destinations that comply with an acceptable-use policy and advertise only tagged routes to commercial or external sites, instead of maintaining a large prefix and AS path filter database. Aggregation is a second use: component prefixes that form an aggregate are only useful to the neighboring peer, so they can carry a community value the neighbor matches and filters on, which keeps them from spreading beyond their desired scope.
sections.plainLanguage: BGP routers once matched long lists of addresses to decide what to share. This RFC lets an operator put one tag on a group of destinations and write the policy rule once, against the tag.

sections.title: The COMMUNITIES Attribute
sections.content:
The RFC creates the COMMUNITIES path attribute: an optional transitive attribute of variable length, with Type Code 8. It holds a set of four-octet values, and every route carrying the attribute belongs to the communities listed in it.

Communities are treated as 32-bit values. For administrative assignment, two ranges are reserved: 0x0000000 through 0x0000FFFF, and 0xFFFF0000 through 0xFFFFFFFF. All other values are encoded with an autonomous system number in the first two octets. The meaning of the final two octets is defined by that autonomous system. For example, AS 690 may define its own community values from 0x02B20000 through 0x02B2FFFF.
sections.plainLanguage: Each community is a 32-bit code attached to a route. The first half of the code names the autonomous system that defined it, and the second half means whatever that autonomous system says it means. Two ranges of codes are reserved.

sections.title: Well-known Values and Operation
sections.content:
Three well-known communities have global significance, and any community-aware BGP speaker must implement them. NO_EXPORT (0xFFFFFF01) means routes must not be advertised outside a BGP confederation boundary. NO_ADVERTISE (0xFFFFFF02) means routes must not be advertised to any other BGP peer. NO_EXPORT_SUBCONFED (0xFFFFFF03) means routes must not be advertised to external BGP peers, including peers in other member autonomous systems inside a confederation.

A speaker may use the attribute to control which routing information it accepts, prefers or distributes. A speaker that receives a route without the attribute may add it when passing the route on, and may modify the attribute by local policy. If routes are aggregated and the result does not carry the ATOMIC_AGGREGATE attribute, the aggregate should carry all communities from all of the aggregated routes. The attribute works with BGP version 2 and later versions. The RFC states that security issues are not discussed.
sections.plainLanguage: Three tag values have the same meaning in every network: do not export this route, do not advertise it to any peer, or keep it inside the confederation. Routers can also add, change or filter tags under their own policy.

items.label: NO_ADVERTISE
